chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Poverty almost becomes disbelief, and envy almost overcomes destiny.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith 'Poverty almost becomes disbelief'?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith links material deprivation to spiritual vulnerability, suggesting that extreme poverty may drive a person to deny God’s providence, a concept echoed in Shia tafsir as 'kufr al-ni‘mah' (denial of blessings). Furthermore, it posits that intense envy (hasad) can act as a causal force capable of altering or delaying divine decree (al-qada’), illustrating the dynamic interplay between human agency and destiny.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The poverty can almost cause one to be a disbeliever, and the envy may almost overcome (disable) the power of an envying person’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
‘‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Poverty can almost be disbelief, and envy may almost overcome (disable) the power of an envying person.’”
